newsitem.title: USA: Northwest pulls ads with toddlers, buckets.
newsitem.headline: Northwest pulls ads with toddlers, buckets.

text.p: The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission said Friday that at its request, Northwest Airlines Corp was pulling an advertisement in USA Today showing a child bending over with its head in a bucket.
The airline, said the commission, agreed to pull the ad and to mount a safety campaign after the CPSC advised it that about two children die each month in the U.S. by drowning in buckets.
"Northwest Airlines has been extremely cooperative," said CPSC chairwoman Ann Brown. "It is in the same position as many parents -- it simply didn't know about this deadly hidden hazard.
But it has agreed to act quickly, to pull the ad and to mount a safety campaign to let more people know about the drowning danger to children posed by buckets."
From January 1984 to March 1997, the CPSC said it received reports of 293 children drowning in buckets. In 1995 alone, the last year for which there is complete data, 29 children died this way.
